content.title: Gate reviews refused for decision "approved": reviewer-facing docs never state the literal "approve" or show an approving example
content.observation: The engine refused two technical-reviewer gate reviews with the same schema error, `$.decision: must be one of approve, changes_requested (got "approved")`: the design re-review (event:128) and the plan re-review (event:160). Both were the reviewer's first approving review on that gate; its earlier changes_requested reviews (event:106, event:148) were accepted. Each time the reviewer resubmitted with "approve" about 3 s later (event:129, event:161), so the cost was one refused review per approval plus a review.rejected count in metrics, not a wrong decision. A recorded check (ev:ev-muyo96d3-01a13297) shows what the reviewer was given: (1) skills/review-gate/SKILL.md has one JSON example and its decision is "changes_requested". It never states the literal `approve`, and its prose says "approval" and "to approve". (2) templates/review.json gives the pipe placeholder "approve | changes_requested". That is not itself a valid value, which is fine because it forces a choice, but it is the only place the token appears. (3) agents/technical-reviewer.md says only "Approve only when everything is met. Otherwise request changes." and never names the field value. agents/security-reviewer.md never mentions `decision` at all. (4) agents/architecture-reviewer.md does state "`decision`: `approve` only if ...". The architecture-reviewer's approve (event:59) was accepted on the first try. That contrast is a single data point (n=1 against n=2) and a correlation, not a controlled comparison. The docs gap is confirmed deterministically. That the gap caused the "approved" spelling is inferred: it fits the evidence, but no experiment isolated it.

occurrences.note: technical-reviewer, design gate re-review: decision "approved" refused by schema; accepted as "approve" at event:129 (+3 s).

technical-reviewer, plan gate re-review: same error, same reviewer role, about 18 min later; accepted as "approve" at event:161 (+3 s). The first occurrence did not prevent the second, so there is no carry-over between reviewer invocations.

content.recommendation: Make the exact enum value explicit where reviewers decide. This is a docs-only change; do not loosen schemas/review.schema.json to accept "approved" as an alias, because that is an approval-rule change. (a) skills/review-gate/SKILL.md, step 4: directly after the existing example add: "`decision` must be exactly `\"approve\"` or `\"changes_requested\"`. Any other string (`approved`, `approval`, `reject`) is refused as a schema error." Then add, under step 5, a complete approving re-review example in a ```json block with "decision": "approve", all criteria met: true with ev: evidence, "findings": [], and a resolvedFindings entry. (b) agents/technical-reviewer.md, section "Write the review": replace "Approve only when everything is met. Otherwise request changes." with the wording already used in agents/architecture-reviewer.md: "`decision`: `approve` only if every criterion is `met: true` with evidence and no blocking or major finding is open. Otherwise `changes_requested`, with at least one `blocking` or `major` finding. These are the only two accepted values." (c) agents/security-reviewer.md, section "Rules": add the same `decision` bullet. Keep the templates/review.json placeholder invalid, because a valid default could let a review approve without an explicit choice. Evaluation: `node .eccode/drafts/check-review-decision-docs.js` (from the project root) exits 1 today and should exit 0 after the change. For regression, the schema enum is unchanged, "approved" is still refused, and the toolkit test suite passes. Measure the effect by counting decision-enum review.rejected events in later deliveries.
appliesWhen: A reviewer agent writes gate-review JSON validated against schemas/review.schema.json (decision enum approve | changes_requested)
review.rejected events whose reason starts with `$.decision: must be one of` (for example got "approved" or "approval")
Reviewer-facing docs (agents/<reviewer>.md, skills/review-gate/SKILL.md) describe the decision in prose ("approve", "approval") without stating the literal field value or showing an approving example
Any other agent-authored JSON whose enum value differs from the natural-language past tense (verify vs verified, approve vs approved) and whose docs give only a placeholder
notApplicableWhen: review.rejected for other reasons (unmet criteria, unresolved findings, missing reviewer-run check, changed artifacts); those are substantive refusals, not a wording mismatch

Docs already state the literal `approve` and show an approving example (the check exits 0) and the error still recurs; look for another cause, such as a stale cached copy of the docs or a different template source
A proposal to change the schema or the engine's accepted values: out of scope for a docs/skill improvement

revisions.reason: environment.toolkit was a free-text key the env check cannot verify, so search reported DOES-NOT-APPLY everywhere; the lesson is not environment-dependent, so environment is {}

reviews.notes: Independently verified. (1) Occurrences: event log has exactly two decision-enum review.rejected events, seq 128 (design) and 160 (plan), both technical-reviewer, got "approved", each followed ~3 s later by an accepted approve (129, 161); prevHash chain intact across 203 events (ev:ev-muyocjft-010056eb). (2) Docs read directly: review-gate SKILL.md has only a changes_requested example and never states the literal approve; technical-reviewer.md says only 'Approve only when everything is met'; security-reviewer.md never mentions decision; templates/review.json has the invalid pipe placeholder; architecture-reviewer.md line 32 states the literal; schema enum is [approve, changes_requested]. (3) Re-ran the author's check: exits 1 with 4 gaps matching the docs (ev:ev-muyobxy2-01ca1f8e). Read its source: it derives the enum from the schema, reviewer roles from config, and uses a delimiter-bounded regex so 'approved'/'approver' and the pipe placeholder do not count. Sensitivity: on a scratch copy with the recommended edits applied it exits 0 (ev:ev-muyoc8u1-010a58f5), so it is not a never-passing check. (4) Honesty: confidence low, causation explicitly stated as inferred, n=1 vs n=2 contrast flagged as correlation; recommendation is docs-only, keeps schema strict and template placeholder invalid (no approval-rule loosening) - proportionate. Caveats, non-blocking: an unexcluded contributing cause is that the engine's own state vocabulary is 'approved' (gate status/approvedBy in gate show --json, which reviewers are told to run first) plus a general past-tense prior; appliesWhen item 4 (any agent-authored JSON enum) extrapolates beyond the evidence; check script cosmetic: rejectsBefore unused and the per-gate label prints a total against the global first approve (exit code unaffected).
